components.name: Model API gateway for LLM-as-judge evals

assumptions.subject: workload
assumptions.statement: 6,000 spans/s at peak from instrumented agents: 91% span ingest, 7% trace queries from the UI, 2% of spans sampled for an automated LLM-as-judge eval.

assumptions.subject: store
assumptions.statement: The trace store is a COLUMNAR store (ClickHouse-shaped). v1 has no columnar component kind, so it is modelled as sql_db at 4,000 batched writes/s per node across 2 nodes. Columnar compression and background merge behaviour are not represented.

assumptions.subject: proc
assumptions.statement: 700 spans/s per enrichment instance: JSON parse, PII redaction, and token/cost attribution per span on 2 vCPU. This tier is the bottleneck - enrichment, not ingest, is what an agent-observability stack scales on.

assumptions.subject: blob
assumptions.statement: 35% of spans carry a payload large enough to offload (full prompts and completions, about 8 KB), kept for 90 days. Object-store capacity is about 5,500 GET/s per S3 prefix; instances here mean PREFIXES, not servers.

assumptions.subject: judge
assumptions.statement: The judge model provider is modelled as the model API gateway that fronts it (v1 has no per-instance price for an external API). Capacity is provisioned quota: 3 pools x 4,000 requests/minute, about 201 calls/s. Judge calls are 2,500 input / 200 output tokens (trace plus rubric in, a score and a reason out).

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: Prompt caching is not modelled, and the columnar store's own disk is not priced (the engine's only storage rate is object storage). Both make the shown bill incomplete: the token line is an upper bound, the storage line a lower one.

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: SPAN INGEST IS INBOUND AND FREE - only the ~256 B acknowledgement egresses. The billed egress is the UI reading traces (~16 KB per trace query). Charging egress on ingest volume would have roughly doubled this line for no reason.

assumptions.subject: cost
assumptions.statement: The model gateway carries NO compute and NO per-request charge: v1 has no per-instance price for this kind, and a self-hosted proxy has no per-request SKU, so inventing either would be worse than the gap. Its whole cost line is the provider token spend.

assumptions.subject: engine
assumptions.statement: Ingest burstiness is not expressible in v1: the engine simulates a steady arrival rate, while real OTLP traffic arrives in batch spikes that the Kafka buffer exists to absorb. The buffer's value is therefore invisible in these numbers.

_library.summary: Trace, cost-attribute and auto-evaluate LLM agent runs: OTLP ingest, a buffered enrichment pipeline, a columnar trace store and sampled judge evals.
